claims.content: To report ballistic missile surveillance tracks/points on the interface so that C2 JU provides complete, accurate, timely, correlated information in accordance with R2 reporting rules.

goal.raw_text: To report ballistic missile surveillance tracks/points on the interface so that C2 JU provides complete, accurate, timely, correlated information in accordance with R2 reporting rules.

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU has R2 for the ballistic missile track to be reported.
For an initial surveillance report on a ballistic missile, the predicted time to impact is not less than 16 seconds.
For an initial Ballistic Missile surveillance report on a descending ballistic missile, the altitude of the descending ballistic missile is not less than 8 data miles.
When a related TN for an Impact Point is used, the C2 JU has R2 for the related missile track.
The local ballistic missile track to be reported is uncorrelated with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.
The C2 JU determines that a locally derived ballistic missile track is uncorrelated with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.

trigger.raw_text: The C2 JU determines that a locally derived ballistic missile track is uncorrelated with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.

claims.content: C2 JU determines whether the data points being detected by its local sensors are currently reported on the interface.
C2 JU continuously correlates locally derived ballistic missile tracks with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.
C2 JU reports on all uncorrelated local ballistic missile tracks and assumes R2 for those tracks in accordance with the R2 rules as specified in paragraph 4.4.6.15.
C2 JU transmits J3.XC1 at next opportunity for new tracks when assuming R2 or when data changes.

C2 JU reports positional data for ballistic missile tracks in the Space Track message as X, Y, Z position in earth-centered, earth-fixed (ECF) Cartesian coordinates defined by the World Geodetic System-84 (WGS-84) Reference Frame.
C2 JU reports the velocity of ballistic missile tracks as the rate of change along the X, Y, Z axis.
A JU with R2 of a ballistic missile track maintains R2 on the related Impact Point.

C2 JU uses the J3.0 Reference Point message to report the actual or expected Launch Point of a ballistic missile; the time of the launch is reported to the nearest second with the Time Function field set to value 4, Departure Time.

At main flow step 1, if there are conflicts between locally derived information and information reported on the interface, C2 JU shall resolve the difference by transmitting the appropriate J7 message, by operator procedure, or by voice coordination.

At main flow step 3, if a C2 JU with R2 for the Reference TN receives a J7.1 message with the Data Update Request Action field set to value 2, Ballistic Missile Update Request, on a specific TN, the JU shall respond with a J3.6 Space Track message and transmit the data held in the appropriate J3.6 word sequence.
During execution of a DUR response, if an R2 shift occurs where the Number/Frequency of Updates field is set to value 2 or 3, the JU assuming R2 shall not respond to any prior Data Update Request.
At main flow step 6, after predicted impact, there is no requirement to continue transmitting a missile impact point.

If the predicted time to impact is less than 16 seconds, the JU shall not transmit an initial surveillance report on a ballistic missile; if the altitude of the descending ballistic missile is less than 8 data miles, an initial Ballistic Missile surveillance report shall not be transmitted. Impact points are not subject to this constraint. Exit: do not transmit the initial report.

If there are conflicts between locally derived information and information reported on the interface, the C2 JU shall resolve the difference by transmitting the appropriate J7 message, by operator procedure, or by voice coordination. Exit: conflict resolved by one of these means.

If differences in ballistic missile position or velocity are recognized by a JU, those differences are not resolved through conflict processing and shall not generate a J7.0 message with the Track Management Action field set to value 1, Difference Report; refer to Resolution of Duplicate Track Number, paragraph 4.1.3.7. Exit: do not use conflict processing or generate a Difference Report.

If a non-R2 JU receives a J7.1 message with the Data Update Request Action field set to value 2, Ballistic Missile Update Request, on a specific TN, the JU shall not respond. Exit: no response to the J7.1 (ACT = 2) request.

If an R2 shift occurs during execution of a DUR response where the Number/Frequency of Updates field is set to value 2 or 3, the JU assuming R2 shall not respond to any prior Data Update Request. Exit: do not respond to any prior Data Update Request.
There is no requirement to continue transmitting a missile impact point after predicted impact. Exit: no requirement to continue transmitting a missile impact point after predicted impact.
The C2 JU reports on all uncorrelated local ballistic missile tracks and assumes R2 for those tracks in accordance with the R2 rules specified in paragraph 4.4.6.15.

The positional data for ballistic missile tracks are reported in the Space Track message as X, Y, Z position in earth-centered, earth-fixed (ECF) Cartesian coordinates defined by the World Geodetic System-84 (WGS-84) Reference Frame.
The velocity of ballistic missile tracks is reported as the rate of change along the X, Y, Z axis.

The J3.0 Reference Point message is used to report the actual or expected Launch Point of a ballistic missile; the time of the launch is reported to the nearest second with the Time Function field set to value 4, Departure Time.

If a conflict existed between locally derived information and information reported on the interface, the C2 JU has resolved the difference by transmitting the appropriate J7 message, by operator procedure, or by voice coordination.
